correctness.summary: Cauchy interlacing between W_k, its point-deleted principal subgraphs, and the fixed induced Kneser graph KG(k,2) pins down all three inertia counts. A separate elementary argument proves connectivity and reducedness. The Kneser inertia used in the proof is derived directly from the point--2-subset incidence matrix.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Akbari et al. explicitly ask for an infinite reduced equality family. Chen and Li construct W_k and analyze the special deletion W_5-a_1, but the checked sources and targeted searches did not locate the general point-deletion formula, the interval realization consequence, or the all-k equality subfamily. Residual risk remains from very recent or differently indexed work.

value.summary: The theorem turns the Chen--Li counterexample family into an exact inertia ladder, realizes a full interval of positive inertia values for every negative index q>=4, and supplies an infinite family answering the explicit equality-family question in Akbari et al.

limitations: The theorem does not determine the maximum possible positive inertia for fixed negative inertia.
No classification of all reduced equality graphs is claimed.
Point deletion from W_k is not claimed to be the unique construction producing equality.
Finite verification is supporting evidence and not part of the proof.
Originality is to the best of our knowledge and retains residual risk from very recent or differently indexed work.
